title: Open models do most of the work. Closed models still get paid
dek: Open-weight AI now handles most developer tokens and runs about four months behind the frontier. It wins on price for some jobs but not all. Here's how to choose.
tldr: Closed models still hold the top spot: Claude Opus 5.5 scores 58 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, and the best open model, Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Pro, scores 46 [^1] [^2].
The gap is about four months. Open models match what closed models could do a season earlier [^3].
In August, open-weight models ran 56% of tokens on Vercel's AI Gateway but took only 14% of the spend [^4].

sections.heading: Who's on top this month
paragraphs: Closed models still lead on raw capability. Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 58. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, launched September 3, is next at 53, and Meta's proprietary Muse Spark 1.3 follows at 48 [^1] [^4].

The open-weight pack is close behind and crowded. **Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Pro (46)**, Z AI's GLM-5.3 (45) and Moonshot's Kimi K3 (44) are the strongest models you can download and run yourself [^2]. They score level with SpaceXAI's Grok 4.7 and Alibaba's closed Qwen3.8 Max [^1].
Google's highest-ranked current model on the index is Gemini 3.8 Flash at 41 [^1]. The index weighs agentic and knowledge-work tasks heavily, so treat it as one lens, not a verdict.

sections.heading: The gap is measured in months, not years
paragraphs: Epoch AI finds that since January 2026, the best open-weight models have trailed the best closed models by **about four months** on its capabilities index. That's slightly more than the three-month lag it measured through October 2025 [^3].
Epoch also warns that the figure probably understates the real distance. Open models tend to optimize for public benchmarks, while closed labs hold back their strongest internal systems [^3].

Mozilla's State of Open Source AI report makes the gap concrete. It fits a lag of about 4.4 months on METR's task-length data: closed models can handle 8 to 12 hour tasks, and open models get there about four months later [^5]. For most everyday work, that gap doesn't matter. For the hardest, longest tasks, it does.

sections.heading: Open isn't automatically cheaper
paragraphs: Price per token is the wrong number to compare. What matters is **cost per task**, which depends on both the price and how many tokens a model burns thinking. Among models scoring 44 to 46 on the index, cost per task runs from $0.13 to $5.41 [^1].

The cheapest is open: MiMo-V2.6-Pro, at $0.13 [^1]. But GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3, both open, cost about $2 per task, more than twice the $0.82 of GPT-6 Astra on its low setting, which is closed and scores higher (46) [^1]. Run your own workload through both kinds before assuming that open saves money.

sections.heading: Open models win the volume, closed models win the money
paragraphs: On Vercel's AI Gateway, open-weight models went from 7% of tokens in December to 13% in April and **56% in August**, the first month they carried the majority. But they accounted for only 14% of spend, and Anthropic alone kept 64% [^4]. Teams send bulk work to cheap open models and pay for closed ones where quality matters.

OpenRouter shows the same pattern. Eight of its top ten models by token volume in August were open-weight, and seven of those eight were built in China [^5]. On August 3, DeepSeek became the first open-model maker to rank first on the platform by requests [^5].

Deployment is the bottleneck. Developers take open models to production 12 percentage points less often than closed ones, and Mozilla's survey with SlashData traces the gap to tooling, not capability [^5]. Enterprise spending still leans heavily closed: as of December 2025, open-source models had just 11% of enterprise LLM usage, down from 19% [^6].

sections.heading: How to choose
paragraphs: Open weights mean you can download the model, host it on your own infrastructure and fine-tune it [^2]. Closed models give you the frontier and a managed service. Most teams will end up using both.

takeaways: **Route by difficulty.** Send bulk, routine work to open models and escalate to closed ones for the hardest tasks. That's what gateway traffic already shows teams doing [^4].
**Benchmark cost per task, not price per token.** Open and closed models at the same score differ by more than 40x in cost [^1].
**Budget for tooling.** The main thing keeping open models out of production is tooling, not model quality [^5].
**Re-test every quarter.** With a gap of about four months, today's closed-only capability is likely to be available open by early 2027 [^3].
**Mind where your model comes from.** Seven of the eight most-used open models on OpenRouter are Chinese-built, so check the licence and your compliance requirements before deploying [^5].
